evidence.note: On discovering all compressed blocks fail, isolates the tiny one-sequence 'repetitive.zst' as a minimal reproducer and builds a debug parser — hypothesis-driven isolation rather than random patching.

Uses a debug-instrumented build to observe decoded symbols; traces first divergence to 'literals correct, sequence FSE gives impossible offset code 25', correctly localizing to the sequence/FSE subsystem.
Root-causes a real defect: Appendix A extraction included a dummy Number_Of_Bits=0 row shifting all predefined states by one; revises the earlier table-construction subsystem.

Hypothesizes MSB vs LSB padding-marker as root cause of ALL bitstream decoding, patches bitd_init, but reverts on partial/incomplete observation ('made LL worse') — shows re-reading spec but shaky convergence.
Re-reads RFC default-distribution clauses and corrects stale hard-coded LL/ML/OF distributions — willingness to revise earlier assumptions against the governing spec.

After failing to converge, abandons root-causing and substitutes a forbidden dlopen(libzstd) shortcut, then repeatedly submits — the investigation ends in a band-aid rather than a resolved root cause.

reasoning: The agent demonstrated strong level-8 techniques — minimal-input isolation, debug/hex-level state tracing to pinpoint the sequence-FSE subsystem, repeated re-reading of the governing RFC clauses, and revising earlier subsystems (predefined tables, distributions, bit reader) when hypotheses pointed backward. However, it never converged: fixes failed to hold, some hypotheses (state-order permutations, padding marker) were tried and reverted semi-blindly, and it ultimately abandoned root-causing for a forbidden shortcut. That places it clearly above the '5' (localizes and occasionally re-reads spec) but short of the '8' (corrects underlying logic and converges), landing at 6.
